text:
Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo.
It was a remarkable 10th victory in a row in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time.
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafodé Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.
Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Álvaro Rodríguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time.
Rose’s team could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen, 4-0 winners over Benfica on Thursday, in two weeks’ time.
Ruben Amorim’s Milan, who had lost three of their opening four matches, gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos. Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knockout phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Jota Silva’s 49th-minute strike. Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse to equalise in the 63rd minute.
Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth.
